title: Difference between html building rules

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body:
Hi, I want to ask about the difference between the two rules for building a tag.

The **first** is https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/syntax.html#start-tags

The **second** is https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#tag-open-state

The **first** rule says that the tag name must be **ASCII alphanumeric** (_[a-z0-9]_), but does not specify what the first character should be and what subsequent ones.
As for the **second** rule, it accurately speaks for all symbols.

Look here:
If we write such tags: `<mytext>` or `<100mytext>` or `<mytext100>`, this will follow the **first** rule, but `<100mytext>` the browser will consider that he is incorrect and will handle it in a special way.

However, if we look at the **second** rule, we will understand that the characters that can be used in their tags are much larger than in the **first** rule (**ASCII alphanumeric**). Accordingly, we understand that you can write the following tags: `<text#>`, `<text%100>`, `<text?ю>`. In the **first** rule, there was no mention of symbols outside of ASCII alphanumeric, as well as clarification that the **first** character should be **ASCII alpha**.

Explain to me why the **first** rule is needed, because the **second** explains all the rules that are needed.

P.S I think this question is not particularly relevant here. I just do not know where to ask, so that anyone can tell about it clearly.
